The cost of hiring a plumber varies widely depending on location, job type, and urgency. Nationally in the U.S., hourly rates range from $45 to $200, with an average hourly rate of about $105 [d4][d8][d1]. For standard jobs, the average plumbing project costs between $150 and $500, while small repairs (toilets, sinks, faucets) typically run $125–$350 and large repairs $500–$800 [d1][d9]. Emergency plumbing calls are significantly more expensive, averaging $350 per hour plus a trip fee of around $225 [d8]. Regional differences also matter: in Florida, average jobs cost around $309 [d3]; in Texas, total costs range from $180 to $2,000 depending on service type, with hourly rates of $45–$200 [d5]; in Pennsylvania, rates run $90–$250+ per hour with a minimum service call of $200 [d7]; and in the Houston area, specific repairs like faucet repair cost $300–$900 and garbage disposal repair $150–$250 [d6]. For major projects, installing new plumbing in a single room averages ~$1,200, and replumbing an entire house can cost $6,095–$20,000 [d8]. When hiring, it is advisable to get at least three estimates, verify licensing and insurance, and avoid paying large sums upfront [d9].
